topics.title: The greatest of all: common factors and HCF

concepts.learning_objective: Find the common factors of two numbers by listing the factors of each.
Explain the Highest Common Factor (GCD) and use it to solve tiling, packing and jump problems.
Write a number as a product of primes and recognise that the prime factors are unique apart from order.
Use the division method to find the prime factorisation of a number.
Construct the factors of a number from subparts of its prime factorisation.
Recognise a conjecture and disprove a false one with a counterexample.

topics.title: Finding the HCF using prime factorisation

concepts.learning_objective: Find the common factors and HCF of numbers as common subparts of their prime factorisations.
Find the HCF by taking each common prime the minimum number of times it occurs.

topics.title: Least, but not last: common multiples and LCM

concepts.learning_objective: Find the LCM as the lowest common multiple and apply it to repeating-event problems.
Find the LCM by taking each prime the maximum number of times it occurs in the factorisations.

topics.title: Patterns and properties of HCF and LCM

concepts.learning_objective: Make and justify general statements about the HCF and LCM of special pairs of numbers.
Find the HCF when numbers are doubled or are multiples of the same number.

topics.title: Efficient procedures and the HCF-LCM product property

concepts.learning_objective: Use the joint division procedure to find both the HCF and the LCM of two numbers.
Use the relation HCF x LCM = product of the two numbers.
